precepts.text: Seek the kingdom of heaven first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That's what the Bible says.
precepts.point: Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can't grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs or careers is just for us to get by in this captivity. It should not be a focal point in your life. Matthew 6:33, I believe it is. Seek the kingdom of heaven first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That's what the Bible says. So look what it says. What verse was that? Verse eight. Verse nine.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Solomon says “I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can’t grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs and careers are just for us to get by in this captivity; they should not be the focal point of your life. That is Matthew 6:33: seek the kingdom first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That’s what the Bible says.

“Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” That does not mean you just pray, God, give me understanding so I can break down Revelation. You pray to God, and God will tell you to study to show thyself approved and rightly divide the word. You have to choose this, and make him first.

“All gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.” Why is wisdom better than gold and silver? Those things are corruptible: they can be stolen or destroyed, and when you sell them the money runs out quick. Wisdom never runs out, because with wisdom you get the understanding to make more and to do this and that.

“I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” I choose wisdom above all things; I prefer the Lord above all things. If you want understanding, call upon God and he will give it, but we have to make him first. Wisdom is “a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God”, and seeking that first is the beginning of the transition from milk to meat.

precepts.text: For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness. For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her. For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. That is the glass. She is the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and this Bible is the image of his goodness.
precepts.point: For now we see through a glass, darkly. So what is the glass referring to?

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Paul says “For now we see through a glass, darkly”. What is the glass? Wisdom of Solomon answers it. “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Keep in mind the whole time that we are talking about the glass.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom is the breath and the power of God. “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”. That is the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God.

“and the image of his goodness”: this Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. The mirror itself is unspotted, but we see into it darkly. We do not have all of it fully. We know in part and we prophesy in part, even Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he did not show many of the other apostles.

That is meant to humble us. We have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this book we do not fully understand, so you do not know as much as you think you know. When that which is perfect is come, Christ, that which is in part shall be done away, and then we shall see face to face.

precepts.text: Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect. So the wisdom that we are speaking among these people out here that think they have got some real wisdom. Yet not the wisdom of this world. We do not speak their wisdom. We speak God's wisdom. God's commandments. That is how we speak. Nor of the princes of this world. We do not speak the wisdom of the princes of this world. Their wisdom is not God's wisdom. That come to nought. That come to nothing. The Lord is going to bring all that wisdom down. It is our wisdom that is going to be raised up in authority in this society.
precepts.point: For in her is an understanding spirit, holy, one only, manifold, subtle, lively, clear, undefiled. The wisdom of God is undefiled. Plain, not subject to hurt. It is not subject to hurt. Loving the thing that is good, quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good. The wisdom will lead us to be proper in everything, everywhere we seek to move, everything that we seek to endeavour, everything that we seek to make happen. Wisdom will properly guide us. Not just any kind of wisdom. God's wisdom. I have got to clarify that.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
Wisdom is “loving the thing that is good quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good”. That wisdom will properly guide us in everything we seek to move in, every endeavour, everything we seek to make happen. But not just any kind of wisdom: God’s wisdom. Paul makes that clear.

“Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect”. We speak wisdom among these people out here who think they have some real wisdom. “Yet not the wisdom of this world”: we do not speak their wisdom. We speak God’s wisdom, God’s commandments; that is how we speak.

“Nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought”. The wisdom of the princes of this world is not God’s wisdom, and it comes to nothing. The Lord is going to bring all that wisdom down, and it is our wisdom that is going to be raised up in authority in this society.

That is the difference between God’s wisdom and what we learned under Christianity, clapping with a Bible while learning nothing about ourselves, our condition, our deliverance or our salvation, and still having white supremacy on the mind. The wisdom of this world taught us to look at ourselves as nothing, and everything behind that was destroyed. God’s wisdom is “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” That breath has to come in, as in Ezekiel 37 when “the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army”, and undo all that damage.

precepts.why:
Wisdom “is the breath of the power of God.” The power of God is the word of God, and the word of God is wisdom. They're all synonymous; they all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means. That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. He is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. It's an oxymoron. Yet the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them to the point that it has been said that if you keep the commandments, you're sinning. Your church made you dumb as hell.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook. It will affect you to the deepest part of your thought process. It cuts, until you feel sick to your stomach, an emptiness like hunger. If you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” If you are tethered to Christ, you have to be tethered to wisdom, and if you are tethered to Christ and to wisdom, you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak. You hear the pity party you've heard a thousand times before. You tell a man, stop talking, and he keeps talking, explaining, digging the ditch deeper, thinking he's making sense and embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but for the most part, tethered to wisdom, you understand false speech.

“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” Why is one meat better than another? Because you can taste it. You have a palate, and you can say, I like this one better than that one.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” The same way your palate can taste which meat is better, a heart of understanding can discern false speech. You listen to somebody and you know: this is BS. It happened recently, around Passover, talking to a brother: listening for a while, it didn't add up, it started to sound like murmuring. You would have been better off keeping quiet, but being that you want to talk, go ahead and embarrass yourself.

That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7 is describing. Wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.” If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern and understand why people do the things they do: the defense mechanism, the gaslighting, the one in error trying to tug on your heart and make you feel guilty so you will chase him. That's not how this goes. He is supposed to wear down the footsteps.

precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2; it was wisdom, so that we should know better. And what is pure? “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” It will enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you're going in the wrong direction. It's supposed to light your path.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweet, but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That's all right, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul isn't getting converted.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. And converting doesn't just happen; you don't close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults”: things people don't know I'm dealing with. Sometimes a class comes out talking right about you. You said you wanted wisdom. And if it comes in English and you speak Spanish, don't worry: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” We'll translate it, even into sign language. If it's for you, you'll get it. But you need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me.” This is a prayer we ask God for, and then he sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Don't ask for rain and get mad when it's muddy. You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed. The first key is listening. The greatest gift a young person can have is to listen: be neutral, hear what's being said, examine yourself whether it's true, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn what the will of God is, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says.

precepts.text: Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It is supposed to kill the old man in you, not you. When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptation; it starts unmasking who you are and what we have to fix.

precepts.why:
Converting comes through trial, error and correction, and you're supposed to be happy about the correction. “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness”: when that person is telling you what you're doing wrong, it's a kindness that he does it. “and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”: it's going to be a blessing.

“which shall not break my head.” It isn't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It's supposed to kill the old man in you, not you physically. And people don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, for trials, for tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything's going to be perfect. No: it's going to start unmasking who you are, who I am, and what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are. That is the wisdom that leadeth and directeth the wise, as Solomon says: God directs you away from evil and shows you how to avoid it, and his reproof is how he does it.

precepts.text: Solomon learned wisdom diligently and communicated her liberally; they that use her become the friends of God. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today: God gave him certain knowledge of the things that are, to know how the world was made and the operation of the elements, the beginning, ending, and midst of the times, the alterations of the turning of the sun, the change of seasons, the circuits of years, the positions of stars, the natures of living creatures, the furies of wild beasts, the violence of winds, the reasonings of men, the diversities of plants, and the virtues of roots. We are not on Solomon's level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, but that is what the mustard seed government is going to grow into.
precepts.point: Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end. It behooves us to learn God's laws, commandments, and statutes, because to set up a government you need everything we read at the beginning of class about what a community consists of. God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.text: Sown among thorns: the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lust of other things choke the word. Wisdom is free from those cares, so a man with wisdom does not entertain covetousness.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 says wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from what care? Free from worry and stress, and above all free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches and the lusts of other things deceive you. Life does not consist in the abundance of things; they deceive you and choke the word.

Wisdom is free of those cares. The man that has wisdom is not going to be subject to the riches of this world. God said beware of covetousness, and that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it; I am not going to entertain that.

So it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, because wisdom has “all power, overseeing all things.” Tether yourself to wisdom and you can see clearly, the cares of this world cannot choke the word, and it will not become unfruitful in you.

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 says wisdom is “the breath of the power of God.” What is the power of God? Hebrews 4 answers.

“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” We fought that example of unbelief. If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom. Wisdom is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful.” Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 just said wisdom is “quick”, and “having all power.” The same words. And it is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

The intents of the heart are where sin begins. So we want that pure influence, so that the intents of this mind are not led astray and what guides and directs us is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it is wrong to do that. If we turn aside from that, we are saying we are hypocrites and don’t really believe. God has chosen us, for whatever reason, to give us wisdom. The power of God is the word of God. It is wisdom.

precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Influence means to mold you and direct you. If wisdom is flowing down from the Almighty and it is influencing you, you are connected, tethered, with God. Or something else can be influencing you, and that will not be wisdom; it will be covetousness, lust, whatever it might be. Psalms 19 shows what that pure influence is.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise. “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

That pure influence is the statutes, the laws of God. The commandment is “pure”, and it enlightens the eyes so that we can see clearly.

And if our eyes are enlightened and the Lord has converted us, what are we now? We are new, something different. That is where Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 goes: “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new.”

With the word of God you change into another man. That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 means: “she maketh all things new.” Wisdom will make you new, so you can’t keep doing the same thing.

But if the word is dealing with you and you are still trying to live that old man, still letting that old man tell you what to do, still doing that same stuff, the Lord says, I am going to beat you with many stripes, because I gave you something and you weren’t listening. Much is given, much is required. And don’t think many stripes is a pow pow and that is it. Many in that day will say “Lord, Lord”, and he is going to say, I don’t know you.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”

You keep yourself unspotted from the world by visiting the fatherless and the afflicted, all people afflicted in the mind. But you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, out of whatever she was doing, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, we tether ourselves to God, because flowing down from him is wisdom. You come into this truth not knowing any better, wisdom flows down from God to you, you apply it, and you become new: “she maketh all things new.”

precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 says wisdom, “in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom cannot dwell in a body that is subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. Ecclesiasticus 4:10 shows the conversion of our minds in these last days: when we put our interests over the Lord’s, it distances us from him, and when we put the Lord’s interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother.” That is the opposite of the mindset of a whoremonger, who asks, what can I do to this sister, how can I take advantage of this single mother? The son of the Most High asks, what can I do for this young man to build him up? That is why Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a young man, a child, than to fix a broken old man; the broken old man is the one looking to take advantage.

“So shalt thou be as the son of the most High.” If you go opposite of that, you cannot be the son of the Most High. If you are looking at this sister with lustful eyes, trying to figure out how to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you can’t be the son of the Most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you.

That is the charge on the friend of God and the prophet: to go out and raise up God’s children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Much is given to you, and much is going to be required of you.

precepts.text: I prayed and understanding was given me; I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, esteemed riches nothing in comparison, loved her above health and beauty; all good things came to me with her, and I did not hide her riches.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Solomon tells it himself: “For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out. Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.”

“I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” So the question is: do you prefer God’s wisdom? Do you prefer the Lord over your sensual desires? “all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” Solomon did not care about anything else except wisdom.

“All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them”. Wisdom goes before everything.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” He did not hide his wisdom. Sirach says the same: “refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.” Just as Bishop gets on us all the time, our communication should be in the scriptures. Searching after wisdom is a good thing; that is what we are supposed to do. That is how we should talk, it should be on our minds at all times, and everything should always go back to the scriptures.

precepts.text: He hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, to know how the world was made and the operation of the elements, the beginning, ending, and midst of the times. God showed Solomon how the world was created, where air comes from, the spirit in fire, why the ocean never overflows. The greatest king who ever walked the earth almost was consumed by what he knew, and we have not been shown ten percent of it. Anyone who says he knows everything in the Bible is a fool; the Bishops teach more today because more of the spiritual world opens to them as time goes by.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

precepts.why:
God held Moses by him a long season and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Ezra was not the only one; God showed Solomon the same. “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”.

God showed Solomon how the world was created, from the beginning, when he said let there be light. He showed him how the elements operate: water, air, fire. You breathe the air but do not know where it comes from; ask Solomon. There is a spirit in fire: a little fire can consume a whole place; ask Solomon how. Everything runs to the ocean, yet the ocean never overflows; ask Solomon why. Christ said you cannot even count the hairs on your head. Those things are too heavy for us, but God showed them to Solomon.

The scripture says Solomon had more knowledge than any king before him or after him, the greatest king who ever walked this planet. He knew so much that at the end the knowledge almost consumed him. And he saw the beginning, the middle and the end of time, just as Moses did.

So if a young man says, I know everything in the Bible and there is nothing anybody can teach me, you are a fool. You can spend your lifetime in this book and still not master it. Bishop Nathanyel was not teaching back then the way he teaches today; as time goes by, more of the spiritual world opens to the Bishops. We have not been shown even ten percent of what was shown to Solomon. The waters are rising; just be patient.

precepts.why:
For a maid child the mother is “unclean two weeks, as in her separation”, and continues in the blood of her purifying “threescore and six days”: fourteen days plus sixty six days, eighty days for a daughter.

Solomon describes the birth every man has. “I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth, And in my mother’s womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man.” A full term pregnancy is forty weeks, which is ten months; they say nine months but forget the month of conception. He was compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and when he was born he drew in the common air and cried as all others do.

“For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth. For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out.” Every man, king or not, comes the same way, fashioned in his mother’s womb of seed; and the law of Leviticus 12 is written for the mothers who bear them.

note.label: 1 Kings 4: Government, Peace, and the Wisdom That Excelled All

precepts.why:
Solomon speaks of what the Most High gave him: “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons: The circuits of years, and the positions of stars: The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts: the violence of winds, and the reasonings of men: the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots: And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

The knowledge the Most High bestowed on Solomon exceeded that of all men who walked the earth. That is why “he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.” He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs.

“Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.” Since his wisdom already excelled Egypt’s, we have no need to dabble in Egyptology or any doctrine outside the scriptures given to us.

Wisdom, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, is this Bible, and it is the image of his goodness to his people, the Israelites. That is the goodness that fills the hungry soul and the wonderful works to the children of men that men should praise the Lord for.
